summary: In-flow section whose heading-level trigger shows or hides its content, in a flush divided style for stacked sections or a contained card style.
useWhen: A page, drawer, or settings column has secondary sections that users scan by heading and open on demand.
Several related sections stack vertically and some can start collapsed to reduce length.
A single section of optional detail, such as diagnostics or advanced options, should stay out of the way until requested.
avoidWhen: Sections are peers the user switches between, with one visible at a time; use TabGroup.
The hidden content is critical to completing the task.
The content is a navigation tree or a filter list with its own selection semantics.
The trigger needs to open a floating surface rather than expand in place.

alternatives.when: The user switches between peer views of the same area.
alternatives.reason: TabGroup shows one panel at a time with tab semantics.

alternatives.when: A trigger reveals content that should float over the page.
alternatives.reason: Popover anchors content to its trigger without reflowing the page.

alternatives.when: The section is an editable settings group with view and edit modes.
alternatives.reason: CardSetting owns the view, edit, save, and cancel workflow.

accessibility: The trigger is a native button inside a heading element; choose headingLevel to fit the surrounding outline.
The trigger exposes aria-expanded and controls a labelled region containing the content.
Collapsed content is inert and hidden so it is never focusable or announced.
Interactive trailing content sits outside the trigger button so it keeps its own semantics.
Inactive sections expose aria-disabled and cannot be toggled.
states: open is reflected and mutable: the component toggles it on activation and emits dsToggle with the new state. Owners may also set it directly, for example to make sections mutually exclusive.
flush sections show a bottom divider so stacked sections read as one list; contained sections sit on their own card surface.
Height and content opacity animate on toggle and are removed under reduced motion.
responsiveBehavior: The section fills its container width; heading and description wrap rather than truncate.
Content aligns with the heading text, not the chevron, at every width.

customElements: Set open as a property or attribute; listen for dsToggle for user changes.
react: Pass open to DsDisclosure and update it in onDsToggle when controlling it.
angular: Bind [open] and update it from (dsToggle) when controlling it.

references.label: Storybook flush, contained, trailing, and inactive examples

styling.rationale: The component owns the trigger row, divider, card surface, and expand motion; applications own the content and the space between contained sections.

protected.reason: Divider and card surfaces follow the shared border and elevation recipes; choose a variant instead.
